subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards keep only the full-content CardKit update contract, or should OpenClaw add an explicit opt-in append/transport fallback for deployments where full-content updates are too slow?
rationale: The current code follows Feishu's documented full-text contract and prior truncation fixes, but the newest live repro says coalescing full-content updates did not resolve the multi-minute tail, so automation cannot choose the permanent compatibility and config surface direction.

options.title: Approve Opt-In Fallback
options.body: Keep full-content as the default, but allow a clearly documented opt-in append or non-card transport mode with regression coverage and live proof for both the fast and non-truncating paths.

options.title: Stay Full-Content Only
options.body: Reject append/delta behavior and require a different full-content-compatible latency fix, accepting that affected users may need streaming disabled until then.

options.title: Continue Coalescing PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91943 as the candidate fix only if exact-head live proof shows it materially reduces the long-reply tail despite the latest contrary report.

recommendation.title: Approve Opt-In Fallback
recommendation.body: Keep full-content as the default, but allow a clearly documented opt-in append or non-card transport mode with regression coverage and live proof for both the fast and non-truncating paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata names this handle as the Feishu plugin maintainer, and the decision is Feishu channel behavior rather than core runtime policy.
